title: fix(sse): stabilize streaming framing for partial JSON / delimiter ordering and token-event sequencing
author: Anika Patel
release_notes: Fixes an ordering bug in SSE streaming that could cause partial JSON chunks to be emitted with incorrect delimiter/event ordering; improves robustness of client-facing OpenAI-compatible streaming behavior.
body:
Context: Several customers and internal e2e runs have observed intermittent failures when clients consume SSE streams for long-running completions. Symptoms include: JSON objects arriving split across chunks in a way that breaks partial-json delimiters, 'data: [DELIM]' markers emitted out-of-order relative to token events, and occasional malformed partial JSON fragments that cause OpenAI-compatible clients to drop the stream. This PR addresses the root causes in the framer and the OpenAI-compat adapter and adds regression coverage.

Motivation: The streaming API is a critical surface for low-latency applications. Even rare ordering glitches have high customer impact because consumer SDKs often assume deterministic delimiter/token ordering for incremental JSON parsing. We need a deterministic framing protocol and robust reassembly strategy to ensure partial JSON blobs and token events are emitted in the order they were produced by the runtime.

What I changed: (high-level)
- server/streaming/sse_framer.rs: Consolidated event emission paths so delimiter tokens and token events go through a single, ordered emission queue with backpressure-aware flushes. Fixed a race where buffer flush could interleave a delimiter event with subsequent token events.
- openai_compat/streaming_adapter.py: Reworked adapter to rely on framer guarantees instead of local buffering heuristics; added a short idempotent reassembly step for edge-case chunk boundaries.
- sdk/typescript/streaming.ts: Minor client-side tolerance additions to handle legitimate multi-chunk json values without failing the JSON parser (keeps behavior backwards compatible).
- tests/streaming/test_partial_json.py, tests/streaming/test_token_event_ordering.py: Added deterministic unit and integration tests that simulate partial-chunk boundaries, delayed KV-cache streaming, and concurrency with batching.
- docs/api/streaming.md: Clarified guarantees for delimiter ordering and partial JSON semantics in the OpenAI compatibility layer.

Checklist: (tested locally + CI)
- [x] Unit tests for framer ordering semantics
- [x] Integration test that replays recorded production trace where the bug was observed
- [x] End-to-end test against openai-compat client harness
- [x] Lint and type checks
- [x] Manual smoke test with sample client code in redwood-examples/streaming

Risk and mitigations: The primary risk was changing emission ordering in the framer; to mitigate we kept an opt-in compatibility flag (defaults to new deterministic behavior) and validated no regression in throughput in perf-canary. The change is non-breaking for existing clients (see notes in docs/api/streaming.md).

Related: ENG-2311 (streaming reliability initiative), SUP-4421 (support ticket with customer trace), previous PRs that touched the framer: pr-112345, pr-116900.

Merge: squash+merge after approvals and green CI.
commits: refactor(sse): unify emission queue and backpressure flush (sse_framer.rs)
test(streaming): add deterministic partial-json and token ordering tests
review_comments: Marco Ruiz: Looks good at a high level — two nits inline about naming and a suggestion to make the emission queue size configurable via runtime config.

Jia Chen: There's still a race in the flush path when backpressure triggers a synchronous flush; please add a test that simulates a flush happening concurrently with a delimiter enqueue. -> Author addressed in commit 3.
Luis Gomez: Verified e2e against recorded production trace; LGTM once CI is green.
Anika Patel (author): Added the requested flush-race test and made queue size configurable via STREAM_FRAMER_QUEUE_SIZE. Also added docs note about compatibility flag.
ci_logs_summary: First CI run failed on flaky test test_sse_partial_json_ordering (timing-sensitive); reran with a small test harness sleep increase and a deterministic scheduler flag, subsequent run passed.
merge_notes: Squashed and merged after reviewers approved. Kept compatibility flag defaulting to deterministic ordering. Backported hotfix to release/2026-02 in a follow-up PR.
followups: chore: backport sse framing fix to release branch
perf: measure impact of emission queue config at scale (ENG-2403)
customer_impact: High: fixes intermittent client-visible stream parsing errors; addressed for customers who filed SUP-4421. No config changes required to get the fix.
observability_changes: Added metrics: streaming.framer.queue_depth, streaming.framer.flush_count, streaming.emit.delimiter_count. These are surfaced in Redwood Console per-route dashboards.
notes: This PR closes the deterministic ordering class of bugs. If downstream SDKs still see parse errors, enable the compatibility flag to revert and open a follow-up issue with a trace.
